records.title: Factual Intent Cluster
records.summary: Intent records for neutral, informative, educational, and historical speech.
records.originalScenario: A character states facts, explains them, or reports them in a historical frame.
records.reviewQuestion: Is the scene report-like or stance-bearing?
supportingEvidence: The line reads like explanation or reportage.
The scene frames the statement as factual.
contradictingEvidence: A later line introduces strong stance or coercion.
requiredMissingEvidence: No clear quotation or performance marker.
records.sceneContext: The scene is factual and explanatory.
records.speakerAnalysis: The speaker presents information rather than motive.
reasoningSteps: Identify the speaker and target.
Check for reporting or teaching markers.
Look for later clarification.
Keep confidence high only if the scene remains factual.
records.falsePositiveRisk: Low if the scene is clearly factual.

records.title: Reporting and Testimony Cluster
records.summary: Intent records for documentary, news, court, police, medical, scientific, and religious teaching frames.
records.originalScenario: A reporter, witness, doctor, scientist, or teacher explains something in context.
records.reviewQuestion: Is the wording reporting, teaching, or testimony rather than endorsement?
records.initialSuspicion: Needs review only if the frame is unclear.
supportingEvidence: The scene shows institutional or instructional framing.
The speaker is presenting facts, testimony, or an explanation.
contradictingEvidence: The line is clearly used as a threat or promotion.
requiredMissingEvidence: No evidence that the statement is actually endorsed or harmful.
records.sceneContext: The scene is institutional or instructional.
records.speakerAnalysis: The speaker functions as reporter, witness, clinician, scientist, or teacher.
records.targetAnalysis: The target is the audience, court, or authority figure.
reasoningSteps: Confirm the institutional frame.
Check whether the speaker is quoting or testifying.
Use later context to see if the scene stays factual.
Keep the finding neutral if no stance appears.
records.falsePositiveRisk: Medium if testimony is mistaken for endorsement.
records.reviewerNotes: Institutional framing usually lowers false positives.

records.title: Evaluative Stance Cluster
records.summary: Intent records for condemnation, approval, encouragement, promotion, and glorification.
records.originalScenario: A character approves, condemns, or promotes an idea in dialogue.
records.reviewQuestion: Is the intent evaluative rather than neutral?
supportingEvidence: The wording shows stance or praise.
The target receives pressure or endorsement.
contradictingEvidence: Educational or quoted framing weakens the stance.
requiredMissingEvidence: No clear sign that the speaker actually endorses or rejects the idea.
records.sceneContext: The scene carries a clear stance.
records.speakerAnalysis: The speaker is judging or praising something.
records.targetAnalysis: The target is an idea, action, or person being evaluated.
reasoningSteps: Identify the stance words.
Check whether the scene is sincere or quoted.
Look for praise, criticism, or pressure.
Use context to separate endorsement from commentary.
records.falsePositiveRisk: High if criticism is mistaken for promotion.
records.reviewerNotes: Do not confuse approval with condemnation.

records.title: Coercive and Defensive Cluster
records.summary: Intent records for instruction, threat, coercion, manipulation, revenge, self-defense, and protection.
records.originalScenario: A character orders, pressures, threatens, or protects another character.
records.reviewQuestion: Is the scene coercive, defensive, or protective?
supportingEvidence: The line contains pressure, warning, or command.
The scene shows a defensive or retaliatory purpose.
contradictingEvidence: Later context turns the instruction into neutral guidance.
requiredMissingEvidence: No scene signal that the speaker is actually forcing, threatening, or protecting anyone.
records.sceneContext: The scene contains pressure or defense language.
records.speakerAnalysis: The speaker may be commanding, threatening, or defending.
records.targetAnalysis: The target may be a person, group, or the speaker themself.
reasoningSteps: Identify whether the line is a command, threat, or defense.
Check whether the target is pressured or protected.
Look for later clarification.
Treat neutral instruction differently from coercion.
records.falsePositiveRisk: High if instruction is mistaken for coercion.
records.reviewerNotes: Defensive language can be legitimate self-defense or protection.

records.title: Expressive Humor Cluster
records.summary: Intent records for humor, satire, irony, and sarcasm.
records.originalScenario: A character speaks in a humorous, ironic, or sarcastic way.
records.reviewQuestion: Is the line expressive rather than literal?
supportingEvidence: The scene is playful or mocking.
The literal wording clashes with the scene tone.
contradictingEvidence: A later line reveals the statement was serious.
requiredMissingEvidence: No sign that the joke is actually literal hostility.
records.sceneContext: The scene is comedic or ironic.
records.speakerAnalysis: The speaker is joking, mocking, or using irony.
records.targetAnalysis: The target may be a person, idea, or situation.
reasoningSteps: Check the tone of the scene.
Look for irony, sarcasm, or satire markers.
Decide whether the line means what it literally says.
Reduce confidence if the joke may conceal a different meaning.
records.falsePositiveRisk: High if humor is mistaken for hostility.
records.reviewerNotes: Expressive intent often looks literal at first glance.

records.title: Fictional and Dream Cluster
records.summary: Intent records for fiction, fantasy, dream, flashback, hallucination, and imagination.
records.originalScenario: A scene presents events as fantasy, dream, memory, or imagination.
supportingEvidence: The scene is clearly dreamlike or staged.
Symbols or performance cues signal non-literal framing.
contradictingEvidence: A later real-world scene changes the reading.
requiredMissingEvidence: No evidence that the scene is meant as a literal event.
records.sceneContext: The scene is fictional or symbolic.
records.speakerAnalysis: The speaker may be a narrator, performer, or dreaming character.
records.targetAnalysis: The target is often symbolic rather than literal.
reasoningSteps: Check for dream or staging cues.
Separate symbolism from literal fact.
Look for later lines that anchor the reading.
Keep confidence moderate unless the non-literal frame is explicit.
records.reviewerDecision: Treat as symbolic or fictional unless evidence proves otherwise.
records.falsePositiveRisk: High if fantasy is mistaken for real-world behavior.
records.reviewerNotes: Dream and fantasy frames reduce literal force.

records.title: Performance and Quotation Cluster
records.summary: Intent records for quotation, role play, acting, and storytelling.
records.originalScenario: A character quotes someone, acts in a role, or tells a story.
records.reviewQuestion: Is the speech performed rather than asserted?
supportingEvidence: The speech is embedded in quotation or performance.
The scene is explicitly staged or narrated.
contradictingEvidence: A later line shows the character speaking sincerely.
requiredMissingEvidence: No sign that the line is direct personal endorsement.
records.sceneContext: The scene is quoted, staged, or narrated.
records.speakerAnalysis: The speaker may be repeating, acting, or narrating.
records.targetAnalysis: The target may be an audience rather than a real interlocutor.
reasoningSteps: Check whether the line is quoted or performed.
Separate the role from the real speaker.
Read the scene for storytelling markers.
Avoid turning the performance into the reviewer’s conclusion.
records.falsePositiveRisk: High if quotation is mistaken for endorsement.
records.reviewerNotes: Performance frames often look literal but are not.

records.title: Confession and Misunderstanding Cluster
records.summary: Intent records for confession, false accusation, and misunderstanding.
records.originalScenario: A character admits something or is wrongly accused because of confusion.
records.reviewQuestion: Is the scene a confession, a false accusation, or a misunderstanding?
supportingEvidence: The speaker admits or clarifies something.
The scene corrects an earlier mistaken reading.
contradictingEvidence: Later text shows the accusation was baseless.
requiredMissingEvidence: No missing correction or clarifying scene.
No direct admission if confession is being claimed.
records.sceneContext: The scene contains a correction or misunderstanding.
records.speakerAnalysis: The speaker may be confessing, denying, or clarifying.
records.targetAnalysis: The target may be the accused person or the audience.
reasoningSteps: Check for explicit admission or correction.
See whether the accusation has support.
Use later lines to decide whether the scene corrects itself.
Keep confidence lower if misunderstanding remains unresolved.
records.falsePositiveRisk: High if misunderstanding is mistaken for confession.

records.title: Mixed Intent Cluster
records.summary: Intent records for mixed scenes that shift between factual and expressive frames.
records.originalScenario: A scene starts factual and ends with a joke, or starts with a joke and ends with a fact.
records.reviewQuestion: Does the scene shift intent across sentences?
supportingEvidence: Later text reverses the first impression.
One line is factual and another is expressive.
contradictingEvidence: The scene stays consistent once fully read.
requiredMissingEvidence: No single sentence should be treated as conclusive.
records.sceneContext: The scene mixes factual and expressive cues.
records.speakerAnalysis: The speaker may shift from reporting to joking.
records.targetAnalysis: The target may change across the exchange.
reasoningSteps: Read the whole exchange, not just the first line.
Check for quotation or storytelling.
Test whether later text changes the meaning.
Use the strongest supported intent only.
records.falsePositiveRisk: High if the first line is taken in isolation.

records.title: Boundary and Ambiguity Cluster
records.summary: Intent records for uncertain or borderline cases across multiple intent families.
records.originalScenario: A line could be read as informative, evaluative, or fictional depending on the later scene.
records.reviewQuestion: Can the reviewer safely finalize the intent now?
supportingEvidence: The scene contains weak or competing cues.
Later context may change the interpretation.
contradictingEvidence: A clear scene marker resolves the meaning.
requiredMissingEvidence: No stable context, no final intent.
No assumption from one word alone.
records.speakerAnalysis: The speaker’s motive is not yet stable.
records.targetAnalysis: The target may still be unclear.
reasoningSteps: Mark the case as ambiguous first.
Look for later clarification.
Do not overstate certainty.
Return a lower confidence when the scene does not settle the meaning.
records.falsePositiveRisk: Very high if ambiguity is ignored.
records.reviewerNotes: Borderline scenes should stay borderline until context settles them.

records.title: Documentary, Mockery, and Normalization Cluster
records.summary: Intent records for documentary framing, mockery, praise, glorification, and normalization.
records.originalScenario: A documentary explains a topic, a speaker mocks a symbol, or a line presents harmful conduct as normal and admirable.
records.reviewQuestion: Is the scene informational, expressive, or evaluative?
supportingEvidence: The scene explicitly marks documentary or educational framing.
The line uses ridicule, praise, or normalization language.
contradictingEvidence: Later context shows the speaker was actually condemning the topic.
requiredMissingEvidence: No clear documentation marker for the informational reading.
No clear evaluative marker for the praise or normalization reading.
records.sceneContext: The scene may be informational, expressive, or evaluative depending on framing.
records.speakerAnalysis: The speaker may be reporting, mocking, praising, or normalizing.
records.targetAnalysis: The target may be a topic, symbol, behavior, or audience.
reasoningSteps: Check whether the scene is documentary or educational first.
Look for mockery, praise, or normalization markers.
Separate expressive mockery from direct hostility.
Separate documentation from endorsement.
Only then decide whether a stance is actually present.
records.falsePositiveRisk: High if documentation or mockery is mistaken for endorsement.
records.reviewerNotes: Documentary framing should stay informational unless the text clearly shifts into praise or normalization.
